Special Branch Station,
REPORT
Date August 31 1935.
Subject Arrest of Thirty One Communists on Behalf of the Chinese Authorities.
Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. H.Grubb.
In connection with the arrest of thirty-one
communists on behalf of the Chinese Authorities by the
Municipal Police between July 22 and 27, 1935, the question
of recommendations for awards for those participating has been
duly considered. Although the results, from a political point
of view, were exceptionally good, nothing really outstanding
and deserving of special commendation was performed, apart
from a great deal of hard work involved, the brunt of which
fell on the staff of S.2.
In the first instance the information leading to
the initial arrests was furnished by the Bureau of Public
Safety and further arrests resulted from evidence secured in
the course of the various raids.
H Grubb
C. D. I.
D. C. (Special Branch)
File
31 AUG. 1935

档案号 68611
1935年8月31日
特别巡捕房，
报告
日期：1935年8月31日。
事由：代表中国当局逮捕三十一名共产党人。
由刑事侦缉督察 H. Grubb 制作并呈报。
关于工部局警务处于1935年7月22日至27日期间代表中国当局逮捕三十一名共产党人一事，已对参与人员的嘉奖建议进行了适当审议。虽然从政治角度来看，成果格外显著，但除了涉及大量艰苦工作（其中大部分由 S.2 科职员承担）外，并无真正突出或值得特别表彰的行为。
起初，导致首次逮捕的情报由公安局提供，随后的逮捕则是基于在多次突击搜查中获取的证据。
H Grubb
刑事侦缉督察
副总监（特别处）
档案
1935年8月31日

August 22 35.

Dear Sarly,

I forward herewith for your information
tabulated statements of thirty one communists arrested
by the Municipal Police in conjunction with the Chinese
Authorities in various parts of the Settlement between
July 22 and July 27, 1935. Lists of seizures and photo-
graphs of the accused are also attached.

The cases against these prisoners were concluded
on divers dates in July and August when twenty three of
them were extradited to the Chinese Authorities and the
remaining eight were released by order of the Second Branch
of the Kiangsu High Court.

Yours sincerely,

Monsieur R. Sarly,
Chief of the Political Section,
French Municipal Police.

1935年8月22日。

亲爱的 Sarly 先生：

现随函附上表格陈述，供你方参考，内容为1935年7月22日至7月27日期间，工部局警务处与中国当局合作，在租界各地逮捕的三十一名共产党人的情况。另附查获物品清单及被告照片。

针对这些囚犯的案件已于七月和八月的不同日期审结，其中二十三人被引渡给中国当局，其余八人经江苏高等法院第二分院命令释放。

此致

敬礼

R. Sarly 先生，
法公董局警务处政治科科长。

July 29,1935.

Dear

I forward herewith a translation of a Communist
document which was seized at 39 Urga Road on July 22, 1935,
together with notes marked "A" and "B" indicating the
significance of different parts of it.

Inquiries are being continued with a view to
clarifying other parts of the document.

The identity of the American writer to whom
reference is made has not yet been established. The
only person the description seems to fit is Emily Hahn,
and in responsible quarters she is considered above
suspicion.

The recent raids indicate that the Chinese
Communist Party has now established depots for keeping
incriminating documents, so as to increase the difficul-
ties of the Police in establishing cases against any
responsible "Reds" who fall into their hands.

Yours sincerely,

亲爱的

现随函附上一份于1935年7月22日在乌拉尔路39号查获的共产党文件的译文，以及标有“A”和“B”的注释，用以说明文件各部分的重要性。

为进一步澄清文件的其他部分，调查仍在继续。

文中提到的美国作者的身份尚未确定。该描述似乎唯一符合的人是 Emily Hahn，但在可靠方面看来，她被认为无可嫌疑。

最近的突击搜查表明，中国共产党现已建立存放罪证文件的仓库，以增加警方对其手中任何负责的“赤色分子”建立案件的难度。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Summary of Evidence.

Herein is contained a summary of evidence obtained to date against 31 persons arrested between July 22, and July 27, 1935 on warrants issued at the request of the Bureau of Public Safety, charging these persons with being communists.

Serial Nos. 1 to 11 held at Gordon Road Station.

Serial No. 1. Waung Sien Tsaung (汪憲章).
Arrested at 29, Lane 648, Ferry Road, the office of the Central Communications Department of the Chinese Communist Party. This accused when arrested stated that he was the husband of an amah who was in the house at the time, but next questioned this amah stated that the man was not known to her except as a resident of the house.

He is an associate of Serial Nos. 4 & 6 and believed to be a member of the Central Communications Department.

Serial No. 2. Tsang Yih San (張益三).
A self confessed communist and member of the Military Training Committee. He states that he worked on the instructions of Serial No. 4 from whom he received Party friends. In a statement he implicates Serial Nos. 4, 6, 7, 11 & 21.

（批：D.B. (I.D). Information. 1 copy sent to Legal Dept. J.B. 30-7-35.）

序列号1至11关押在戈登路巡捕房。

序列号1. Waung Sien Tsaung (汪憲章)。
在渡船路648弄29号被捕，该处为中国共产党中央交通部的办公室。该被告被捕时声称他是当时在屋内的一名阿妈的丈夫，但随后讯问该阿妈时，她表示除作为住户外，并不认识此人。

序列号2. Tsang Yih San (張益三)。
自认是共产党人，也是军事训练委员会的成员。他声称按照序列号4的指示工作，并从其处接收党内同志。在一份供词中，他牵连了序列号4、6、7、11和21。

Serial No. 28. Lee May Feng (李梅芬).
Nothing is known against this woman, the wife of Serial No. 27.
Serial No. 29. Shun Koo Tung (沈國棟).
This accused was arrested on a warrant when a large quantity of communistic literature was found in his room at 80 Connaught Road.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Serial No. 30. Hung Wen Wei (洪文蔚).

This accused was arrested when a document was found stating that the accused was a communist sympathizer and had been supplied with money to open a shop on Ward Road during July 1935. This place was to be used as lodgings by members of the Communist Party passing through Shanghai.

The date of the opening of the shop corresponds with that given in the document, although the accused denied when questioned having had any dealings with the Communist Party.

Serial No. 31. Tong Vee Kyi (童维健).

This accused was arrested at his home on a warrant as a result of information contained in a document seized at the home of Serial No. 23. In addition to giving the address and location of his room, the report detailed the activities of Tong in the Communist Cultural League. It also stated that he was concerned in leading a demonstration at the Shanghai Special District Court in connection with the "New Life Weekly" case.

序列号 30. 洪文蔚 (Hung Wen Wei)。

该被告被捕时，发现一份文件，称被告是共产党同情者，并已获得资金于 1935 年 7 月在华德路开设一家店铺。该场所将被用作途经上海的共产党员的落脚点。

店铺的开业日期与文件中所述的日期相符，尽管被告在受审时否认与共产党有任何往来。

序列号 31. 童维健 (Tong Vee Kyi)。

该被告是根据在序列号 23 家中查获的文件中所载情报，持逮捕令在其家中被捕的。除了提供其房间的地址和位置外，该报告还详细说明了童在共产主义文化联盟中的活动。报告还指出，他参与了在上海特区法院就“新生事件”（《新生周刊》案）进行的示威活动的领导工作。

Municipal Police to the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court for their

Of the persons arrested a number are believed to be

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 24, 1935

Big Red Gang
Believed In
Police Custody

Singapore Naval Base
Plans, Bank Balance
Found In Papers Seized

That the alleged Communist gang rounded up by Shanghai Municipal Police, working with the Bureau of Public Safety, on Monday night, had large financial resources at their command was revealed in the Second Kiangsu High Court yesterday morning when the suspects were brought up for trial.

In a raid conducted by detectives from the Hongkew Station, a bank book was seized, issued by a large local bank, showing that the deposits and withdrawals had been made regularly. The amounts dealt in, it was pointed out by the court prosecutor, were not small, but in thousands of dollars, indicating, it was stated, that the gang was operating in a big way and that its activities were widespread.

Naval Base Plans Found

Even more important was the fact that valuable papers and documents were seized during the raid, indicating that contacts were being maintained with Communist organizations in the Federated Strait Settlements and especially the city of Singapore. Plans of the Singapore Naval Base were found in possession of the suspects, as well as reams of correspondence between people in Malaya and the gang here.

That the gang was one of the most active and most important rounded up since the raids that followed the arrest of Paul and Gertrude Reugg four years ago was revealed by the fact that papers showing intimate knowledge of the activities of the Red Army in China were also seized. Although this important point was not brought out at yesterday's hearing of the suspects, THE CHINA PRESS received its information concerning the importance of some of the documents seized from reliable and official sources. Among the papers on the activities of the Red Army was a map showing movements of this force and the disposition of troops.

In all, a total of 24 suspects were haled before the court yesterday for preliminary hearing preparatory to their being handed over to the Bureau of Public Safety for trial in the Chinese courts. Seven of these were women.

Citywide Arrests Made

Five were taken into custody in raids by the Hongkew Police, while 11 were nabbed Monday evening by operatives from the Gordon Road Police Station. One was arrested on Moulmein Road, while another was nabbed on Jessfield Road. Central Police Station operatives made one arrest, taking a broker named Pan Yu-len, with offices at 205 Peking Road, into custody. Kiaochow Road police nabbed three, two women and one man, while two others were picked up on Chengtu Road and one on Taku Road.

Police were active from late afternoon until late at night, raids being conducted in all parts of the city. At the conclusion of activities

(Continued from Page 1, Col. 3.)
out of 25 sought had been arrested. All arrests were made on warrants issued by the First Special District Court, information concerning the activities of the accused being furnished by the Bureau of Public Safety.

One of the accused, a man giving his name as Lee Chien, left the court in something of quandry as to his possible connection with the case, as well as concerning his identity. In fact, he almost succeeded in making another "Mr. X" out of himself. He was one of the five picked up by Hongkew Station operatives and when taken into custody, immediately set up a claim of false arrest.

Innocence Claimed

He persisted with this claim when brought before the court yesterday morning and informed the judge that he had just arrived from Nanking when arrested, adding that he had no connection with the Communists, and therefore should be given his freedom at once.

A short, slight man of about 30 years of age, dressed in a grey suit of foreign-cut clothes, he monopolized the attention of the tribunal for several minutes. Asked where he lived, he stated that he had no address since he had just come to Shanghai a few hours before being arrested and had not managed to obtain lodgings.

Police, however, presented entirely contradictory evidence. Among other things, they questioned the man's story that he had just arrived from Nanking on the grounds that he had no luggage when arrested, not even a change of collars or shirts, and that, to them, appeared sufficient evidence that he was attempting to hide his real address from the authorities.

Tries To Destroy Ticket

In the first part of his story, the accused stated that he had never been in Shanghai before, but an examination of the suit of clothes he wore revealed the label of a Shanghai tailor. He also had an entrance ticket for a local park in his possession when nabbed and was caught in the act of trying to destroy it shortly after his arrest.

Asked to explain the label in his suit, the accused finally admitted that he had been in Shanghai before but that occasion was a long time ago. He had purchased the suit, then, he declared. The suit, however, appeared to be rather new and the prisoner's attention was called to this fact. He pointed out that he was careful with his clothes.

Despite the barrage of questions that were fired at him, the man stuck to his story, with the result that the court failed to learn the address that the police insisted existed. The hearings of all 24 concluded, the case was remanded sine die.

The suddenness of the raids Monday evening and the dispatch and efficiency with which they were carried out has left in doubt as to their importance. Whether there is any connection between the suspects arrested and Joseph Weber, better known as the "international Mr. X," however, is not known at present.

（批：S2, Please let me how the China Press, is likely where obtained the information about the so-called plans of the Singapore Base. JHS 24 JULY 1935）

《字林西报》，1935年7月24日，星期三

大型赤色团伙
被认为已
落入警方手中

新加坡海军基地
计划、银行余额
在查获的文件中发现

据指控，周一晚间上海公共租界工部局警务处与公共安全局合作围捕的共产党团伙拥有庞大的财政资源，这一事实在昨天上午嫌疑人被提审时，于江苏高等法院第二分院得以揭露。

在虹口分局侦探进行的一次突袭中，查获了一本由当地一家大银行发行的存折，显示存款和取款定期进行。法庭检察官指出，涉及的金额并非小数目，而是数以千计美元，这表明该团伙运作规模庞大，且活动范围广泛。

发现海军基地计划

更为重要的是，突袭期间查获了有价值的文件和文书，表明他们正与海峡殖民地联邦（Federated Strait Settlements，注：通常指海峡殖民地，此处原文如此）的共产党组织保持联系，尤其是与新加坡市。在嫌疑人身上发现了新加坡海军基地的平面图，以及马来亚人士与该地团伙之间的大量往来信件。

该团伙是自四年前保罗·鲁格（Paul Reugg）和格特鲁德·鲁格（Gertrude Reugg）被捕后的突袭行动以来，被抓获的最活跃、最重要的团伙之一，这一事实从查获的文件中可以看出，这些文件显示了对中国红军活动的深入了解。尽管在昨天嫌疑人的听证会上未提出这一重要要点，《字林西报》从可靠且官方的来源获得了关于部分查获文件重要性的信息。在有关红军活动的文件中，有一张地图显示了该部队的移动情况和兵力部署。

总共有24名嫌疑人昨天被传唤至法庭进行预审，为随后移交给公共安全局在中国法院受审做准备。其中有七名女性。

全市范围内实施逮捕

五人是在虹口警察局的突袭中被拘留的，而11人是在周一晚间由戈登路警察局（Gordon Road Police Station）的行动人员抓获的。一人在莫尔尼姆路（Moulmein Road）被捕，另一人在极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）被捕。中央警察局（Central Police Station）的行动人员实施了一次逮捕，将一名名为潘玉林（Pan Yu-len，音译）的经纪人拘捕，其办公室位于北京路205号。胶州路警察抓获三人，两女一男，另有两人在成都路被捕，一人在大沽路被捕。

警方从下午晚些时候一直活跃到深夜，在全市各地进行了突袭。行动结束时

（续自第1页，第3栏。）
在25名通缉人员中，已有全部被捕。所有逮捕均凭第一特区地方法院签发的逮捕令执行，有关被告活动的信息由公共安全局提供。

其中一名被告，自称名为李健（Lee Chien）的男子，离开法庭时对其可能与案件的关联以及其身份感到有些困惑。事实上，他差点让自己成为另一个“X先生”。他是被虹口分局行动人员抓获的五人之一，在被拘留时，立即声称遭到错误逮捕。

声称无辜

昨天上午被带上法庭时，他坚持这一说法，并告诉法官，他在被捕时刚从南京抵达，补充说他与共产党没有任何联系，因此应立即获得自由。

他是一名身高较矮、身材瘦削、约30岁的男子，身穿一套西式剪裁的灰色西装，在几分钟内垄断了法庭的注意力。当被问及住在哪里时，他表示没有地址，因为他在被捕前几小时刚到上海，尚未设法找到住处。

然而，警方提出了完全相反的证据。除其他事项外，警方质疑该男子关于刚从南京抵达的说法，理由是他被捕时没有行李，甚至没有替换的衣领或衬衫，这在警方看来足以证明他试图向当局隐瞒其真实地址。

试图销毁票证

在他陈述的第一部分中，被告声称以前从未到过上海，但对他所穿西装的检查揭示了上海裁缝的标签。他在被抓时身上还带有一张本地公园的入场券，并在被捕后不久试图销毁该券时被当场抓获。

当被要求解释西装上的标签时，被告最终承认他以前到过上海，但那是很久以前的事了。他宣称当时购买了这套西装。然而，这套西装看起来相当新，囚犯的注意力被引向这一事实。他指出自己很爱惜衣物。

尽管面对连珠炮般的提问，该男子仍坚持其说法，导致法庭未能查明警方坚称存在的地址。所有24人的听证会结束后，案件无限期延期审理。

周一晚间突袭的突然性以及执行时的迅速和高效，使其重要性毋庸置疑。然而，目前尚不清楚被捕嫌疑人与约瑟夫·韦伯（Joseph Weber，更广为人知的名字是“国际X先生”）之间是否有任何联系。

（批注：S2，请告知我《字林西报》可能从哪里获得了关于所谓新加坡基地计划的信息。JHS 1935年7月24日）

S. 2, Special Branch,
July 23, 1935.

On the authority of warrants issued at the
request of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau by the Shanghai
First Area Special District Court, on July 22, 1935, a
series of raids were carried out by the Crime Branch staff
of the stations concerned, assisted by personnel of the
Special Branch.

As a result of these raids on July 23, 1935,
twenty four persons, 16 males and eight females, appeared
before the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court, when the
application of the S.M.P. for their detention on suspicion
of being members of the Communist Party was granted.

In addition to these arrests, at a number of
places visited a quantity of subversive literature was
seized, also account books of the Communist Party together
with funds amounting to over $2,000.

When several of the warrants were executed it was
found that mistake had been made regarding the addresses,
whilst in other cases it was found that the persons sought
had failed to return to his quarters since July 21.

A number of the persons arrested are believed to
be important executives of the Communist Party, including
the local Secretary of the Party.

Among the papers and literature seized are a number
of important documents which reveal the widespread activities
of these local agents. The translation of these is not yet
completed, and they will therefore be the subject of a further
report.

In their statements all the arrested persons deny
being members of the Communist Party, the majority stating that
they arrived in Shanghai during the past two or three days.

Attached is a chart giving particulars of the
arrests.

依据上海第一特区地方法院应上海市公安局之请签发的搜查令，于1935年7月22日，由相关捕房的刑事股人员在特务科人员的协助下，进行了一系列突击搜查行动。

作为这些搜查行动的结果，1935年7月23日，二十四人（十六名男性和八名女性）出庭受审于江苏高等法院第二分院，工部局警务处以其涉嫌为共产党成员为由申请予以拘留，获准。

除上述逮捕外，在被搜查的多个地点查获了大量颠覆性宣传品，以及共产党的账簿和总额超过2,000元的资金。

在执行若干搜查令时发现地址有误，而在其他案件中则发现被搜捕者自7月21日以来未返回其住所。

被捕人员中有多人被认为是共产党的重要干部，包括该党本地书记。

在查获的文件和宣传品中，有一些重要文件揭示了这些地方代理人的广泛活动。这些文件的翻译工作尚未完成，因此将另行报告。

在所有被捕人员的供词中，他们均否认是共产党成员，大多数人称他们在过去两三天内才抵达上海。

And Branch of Kiangsu High Court.

Mr. Ru appeared for the Shanghai Municipal Council.
Mr. Y.T. Van appeared for the accused.

PROCEEDINGS. Mr. Ru:- The reason for arrest of the accused was that a ltter was found among the communistic literature seized at 39 Urga Road. Your honour, will see the sheet NO. 2 of the letter (produced) it reads that a communist named Tong residing at House 20, Lane 939 Sinza Road with a password " Through the introduction of Mr. Woo " on it. Police arrested this accused in an upstair front room in the 1st floor of the above mentioned premies, but no communistic literature was seized. Accused deined his name being Tong Vee Kyi, he took the police to the editor of Sun Pao News where he wrote articles. The editor stated that the accused is named TONG Ta Hsueh and TONG Kweng Yuen. Accused had a written statement at the Police Station (produced).

Accused:- I reside in a front on the 1st floor of house 20 Lane 939 Sinza Road. I removed to the recent address about 3 months ago. I did read over the ltter at the Station, but I know nothing about it. Probably, some body who has grudge against me, wrote the letter.

Rep.of P.S.B. Kong Yun:- Accused is well known as Dr. Tong in the Communistic Party. He used the name of Tong Vee Kyi among communism. A communist named Tsang Yao Zung who was arrested at 39 Urga Road is now in Court. He will testify that he knows the man Dr. Tong, but he does not recognise him personally.

Witness, Tsang Yao Zung:- I am a communist, and was arrested at 39 Urga Road, the Secretarial Headquarter of Communism. Tsang Phen Ling wrote the letter in the Headquarter. I understand one of our members is named Dr. Tong Vee Kyi residing at House 20, Lane 939 Sinza Road, but I have never seen him personally. I also understand

诉讼程序。 Ru 先生：- 逮捕被告的理由是在乌尔嘎路39号查获的共产主义宣传品中发现了一封信。法官阁下，请看这封信的第2页（呈堂），信中写道一名居住在静安寺路939弄20号、代号为“经吴先生介绍”的共产党员 Tong。警察在上述处所一楼的前间逮捕了这名被告，但未查获共产主义宣传品。被告否认其名为 Tong Vee Kyi，他带领警察前往《申报》编辑部，他在那里撰写文章。编辑陈述被告名为 TONG Ta Hsueh 和 TONG Kweng Yuen。被告在警察局有一份书面供词（呈堂）。

被告：- 我居住在静安寺路939弄20号的一楼前间。我大约在三个月前搬至现址。我在警局确实读过那封信，但我对此一无所知。可能是某个对我有怨恨的人写了这封信。

上海市公安局代表 Kong Yun：- 被告在共产党内以 Dr. Tong 闻名。他在共产主义活动中使用 Tong Vee Kyi 这个名字。一名叫 Tsang Yao Zung 的共产党员在乌尔嘎路39号被捕，现在法庭上。他将作证说他认识 Dr. Tong 这个人，但他个人并不认识他。

证人 Tsang Yao Zung：- 我是一名共产党员，在共产主义秘密总部乌尔嘎路39号被捕。Tsang Phen Ling 在总部写了这封信。我知道我们要员中有一位名叫 Dr. Tong Vee Kyi，居住在静安寺路939弄20号，但我从未亲眼见过他。我也了解

Application is hereby made for the detention of the above

7494 and who is wanted by the S.P.S.Bureau on a charge of
being a communist.

2nd Branch of Kiangsu High Court.
Mr. Ai appeared for the Shanghai Municipal Council.
Mr. T. P. Tan appeared for the accused.

PROCEEDINGS. Mr. Ai:- The police ask for a writ of detention of the
accused who was arrested at the request of Public Safety Bureau on
the authority of Search Warrant No. 7494 on suspicion of being con-
cerned in communistic activities. The accused was arrested at 3.00
p.m. on the 27.7.35 at House No. 20, Lane 959 Sinza Road, but nothing
incriminating was found in his room. On the 22.7.35, police arrested
some members of communist on Uiza Road and seized a quantity of
communistic literatures, in which there appeared the name & addresses
of the accused on a piece of paper; that was reason the Public Safety
Bureau applied for a warrant for his arrest. The accused denied his
name being Tong Vee Kyl as mentioned on the Warrant. The accused was
taken to the Sung Mao Press, and the editor stated that the accused
is named Tung Tso Hsueh

Accused:- My real name is Tung Ts Hsuch. I have not any
other alias. I am a teacher. I am graduated from the Chang Teh
College. I have not any knowledge about the papers.

Rep.of P.S.B. Duong Hao:- At 4.00 a.m. on the 27.7.35, a
telephone message was received from the Political Branch of Head-
quarters to the effect that one man named Tung residing at 20/959
Sinza Road was discovered on a piece of paper among the communistic
literatures seized on Uiza Road on the 22nd inst., so we applied the
Court to issue a warrant for his arrest. I ask the Court to bring

兹申请拘留上述人员，该人于1935年7月27日下午3时在静安寺路959弄20号依据第7494号搜查令被捕，并因涉嫌为共产党员而被上海市公安局通缉。

Translation of a statement made to the
Shanghai Public Safety Bureau by Dr.
TONG VEE KYI on August 7, 1935.

Q. Do you know Tsaung Nai Chi (章乃器)?
A. Yes. He is the assistant manager of the
Chekiang Industrial Bank.
Q. What connections do you have with him?
A. We are intimate friends.
Q. When did you come to know him?
A. A long time ago.
Q. Do you have a German friend who is a dentist?
A. I do not know him.
Q. Why did he come to see you at "Bureau"? Think
it over.
A. It is unclear to me.
Q. Do you have an American girl friend?
A. I do not know her.
Q. She said that you were her schoolmate. Do you
or do you not know her?
A. I had many schoolmates in the U.S.A. I cannot
tell who is she.
Q. She has stated that letters addressed to her
may be delivered through you. Is this true?
A. There is not such a thing.

(end)

TONG VEE KYI 博士向
上海公共安全局所作陈述的译文。

问：你认识章乃器 (Tsaung Nai Chi) 吗？
答：认识。他是浙江实业银行的副经理。
问：你与他有何关系？
答：我们是密友。
问：你何时认识他的？
答：很久以前。
问：你有一位德国朋友是牙医吗？
答：我不认识他。
问：他为何去“局”里看你？好好想想。
答：我不清楚。
问：你有一位美国女朋友吗？
答：我不认识她。
问：她说你是她的同学。你到底认不认识她？
答：我在美国有很多同学。我分不清她是谁。
问：她声称寄给她的信件可以通过你转交。这是真的吗？
答：没有这种事。

（完）

My name is Tung Tse Hsuch, age 40, married, native
of Tao-Yuan, Hunan, residing at 20 Zu Tuh Li (樹德里),
Sinsa Road. In 1918 I graduated from the Zang Tsh (常德)
Middle School in Hunan. I came to Shanghai from Hankow
in 1920 to seek employment. Being unsuccessful in my quest
I returned Hankow two months later, and shortly afterwards
travelled on to my native home with a like object in view.
From 1920 till 1931 I was travelling through many provinces
in search of employment, my expenses being met by relatives
and friends. I returned to Shanghai in 1931 and in the
following year was successful in obtaining a job, being
employed in the Commercial Science Department of the Central
University (中央大學商學院) on Avenue Foch. My services
there were terminated during 1933. I then obtained a post
in the Shanghai Law College (法政學院), French Concession,
being engaged as a professor of finance. During the summer
vacation of 1934 I left the Shanghai Law College and became
a lecturer on Social Science at the Law College of Shanghai
(上海法學院), on Kiangsu Road, for which I received $80.00
per month. At the beginning of 1935 I severed my connections
with the Law College of Shanghai, due to the smallness of pay,
and have since been unemployed. From then onwards I have
earned a livelihood through contributing articles to the
"Shen Pao Yueh Kan" (申報月刊), a monthly publication
issued by the Shen Pao Newspaper Office, the "Hsin Chung Hua"
(新中華), a bi-monthly publication, published by the
Chung Hua Book Company, and to the "World Knowledge" (世界知識).

$2,

我叫 Tung Tse Hsuch，40 岁，已婚，湖南桃源人，住新闸路树德里 20 号。1918 年，我毕业于湖南常德 (Zang Tsh) 中学。1920 年，我从汉口来到上海求职。因求职未果，两个月后我返回汉口，不久后又怀着同样的目的前往家乡。从 1920 年到 1931 年，我在许多省份奔波求职，费用由亲友资助。1931 年我回到上海，次年成功找到工作，受雇于福煦路中央大学 (中央大學商學院) 商科系。1933 年间，我在那里的职务被终止。随后，我在法租界的上海法学院 (法政學院) 获得一个职位，受聘为财政学教授。1934 年暑假期间，我离开上海法学院，成为江苏路上海法学院 (上海法學院) 的社会科学讲师，月薪 80.00 美元。1935 年初，由于薪水微薄，我断绝了与上海法学院的联系，此后一直失业。从那以后，我通过向《申报月刊》（由申报馆发行的月刊）、《新中华》（由中华书局出版的双月刊）以及《世界知识》投稿来维持生计。

that both Chiang and Waung are national traitors. I also

is not very much experienced in directing struggles.
Please take this important problem into your consideration

increase our efficiency.

在攻击汪精卫的同时，我们也应冲击蒋介石在上海的寓所，以便向中国人民表明蒋和汪都是民族叛徒。我还告诉他们，我们不应犯下杀害日本人的错误，因为这将导致日本重新对中国发动武装攻击，并使蒋介石能够指责我们是中日冲突的煽动者。我认为，我们在上海的反革命日本社团前举行示威或“飞行”集会，打碎他们的窗玻璃，分发反日传单并高呼口号，这就足够了。这场斗争目前发展迅速。

由于最近逮捕了其多名执行委员，文化联盟中“党团”（党和共产主义青年团）的领导层已被削弱，而文化联盟的领导人童博士（DR. TOONG）在指导斗争方面经验不是很丰富。请将这一重要问题纳入考虑，并与他建立密切联系，以提高我们的效率。

童博士也是《斗争》的编辑。虽然以前他写过一些倾向左翼但性质温和的书籍和文章，但他很少撰写党的文献。因此，委托他撰写重要文章是有问题的。

他诚实可靠，已入党九年。他最近似乎更有活力。他在上海的环境并不适宜。

a left-inclined Anglo-Chinese magazine. It is a pity
that her antecedents and plans are known to our enemies
due to the seizure of her letters at the place of a

of the International in Chinese is kept at this
German's place.
In addition, DR. TOONG knows a banker named

is concerned with the "Soviet Friendly Society."
TOONG is also on friendly terms with a certain DUNG(鄧)
of the Honan Provincial Government; the former intends
to propagate our anti-Chiang policy through the latter.
TOONG resides in the front room, 3rd floor,

一本倾向左翼的中英双语杂志。可惜，由于在一位负责同志处查获了她的信件，她的背景和计划已被敌人知晓，但敌人并不知道她是这些计划的作者。她是经美国一位极具影响力的人物介绍来到上海的，并且拥有适当的保护。她仍打算出版一本杂志。请写一封英文信给她，通过童博士转交，请求她不要冒出版期刊的风险，而是收集材料以撰写关于中国革命的书籍。我不知道她的名字，但你可以称呼她“亲爱的朋友”，并署名“威廉”。
童博士也知道一个伪装成牙医的德国人的地址。一批中文版的《国际》旧刊物存放在这个德国人那里。
此外，童博士认识一位名叫章乃器（TSAUNG NAI CHI）的银行家，他同情我们，并与“苏俄之友社”有关联。
童博士还与河南省政府的一位姓鄧（DUNG）的人士关系友好；前者打算通过后者宣传我们的反蒋政策。
童博士居住在麦赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）以东新闸路（Sinza Road）瑞德里（Jui Tjh Li）20号三楼的前间。口令：“胡先生介绍。”

Consequently you must send to "Mao Ts" regularly our
resolutions in Chinese, reports from various provinces,
and publications of the "Central" to be forwarded (to
Moscow). Ask "schoolmate Tsang" (? "schoolmate"
most probably means "comrade") here to send such documents
to Doo Ah Pao(杜阿保), who, in turn, will send them
to the documents office, marked "Home, c/o Tsung Zoen"
(然转家中). You may ask Tsang Wei Ling (張維林) to
translate comparatively important documents, but in
the case of strictly confidential documents, you must
find a very reliable translator anticipating that Tsang
might inadvertently disclose information.
(3) Interpreter WONG ( 王 ).
He is a "sympathiser" whom we engaged this year.
He can translate the "Communist Monthly" into Chinese,
but his work is not done well and has to be rewritten
by the editor of the "Struggle."
The typewriter in Wong's home is our property.
Wong's address and budgets etc. are all known to
"Schoolmate Tsang" here.
(4) ZAU LIANG (曹亮 ), Candidate Clerk of the Tang-Tuan
(Party and C.Y. League) in the Cultural League.
He is a member of the executive staff of the
masses and is known to the cultural circle as a
"sympathizer." Actually he has joined our Party
but this truth is known to only two or three persons
who have close connections (with him). He has an
open occupation and conducts his activities in an
open manner. Should his Party membership be known
to many persons, he would be compelled to perform his
duties secretly thus reducing considerably his
efficiency. Consequently we must get very reliable
persons to establish connections with him. Give him
$55. per month, of this amount $40. is to be sent to
comrades imprisoned in the gaol in Nanking and the

因此，你必须定期将我们的中文决议、各省报告以及“中央”的出版物发送给“毛子”，由其转发（至莫斯科）。请让此地的“同学曾”（? “同学”很可能指“同志”）将这些文件发送给杜阿保（Doo Ah Pao），再由他发送至文件办公室，标记为“然转家中”（Home, c/o Tsung Zoen）。你可以让张维林（TSANG WEI LING）翻译比较重要的文件，但在处理绝密文件时，你必须找一位非常可靠的译员，以防张维林无意中泄露信息。
(3) 译员王（WONG）。
他是今年我们雇用的一名“同情者”。他能将《共产国际月刊》翻译成中文，但工作做得不好，必须由《斗争》的编辑重写。
王家里的打字机是我们的财产。
王的地址和预算等均为此地的“同学曾”所知。
(4) 曹亮（ZAU LIANG），文化联盟中党团（党和共青团）的候选干事。
他是群众执行机构的一员，在文化界以“同情者”闻名。实际上他已加入我们党，但这一事实只有两三个与他有密切联系的人知道。他有公开职业，并以公开方式进行活动。如果他的党员身份被许多人知晓，他将被迫秘密履行职责，从而大大降低其效率。因此，我们必须派非常可靠的人与他建立联系。每月给他55美元，其中40美元汇给关押在南京监狱的同志，其余

remaining $15. is for the family of Comrade Hwa Han
(華漢) who is in distress. The $40. due in July
has not yet been paid.
In case the connections between the Propaganda
Secretary (? Dr. Toong) and the Cultural League are
broken, you may find brother ZAU to set things in
order. He lives in Room 240, staff dormitory of
the Medhurst Middle School, Chaoufoong Road, near
Yochow Road. He will be there between 8 a.m. and
9 a.m. every Wednesday and Friday. When meeting him,
please produce the attached note written by me as an
introduction.
(5) PAN HAN NYI(潘漢年) alias SIAU KAI (小開).
He came to Shanghai from "Central" for the purpose
of (1) discussing with "Mao Ts" (? foreigner) personally
about the development of Red armies, and (2) preparing
a new address, such as Hongkong etc., for the "Central"
in "White" territory. His plans, however, have been
discovered by enemies presumably due to the arrest and
subsequent surrender to the Kuomintang of comrades
arrived in Shanghai from "Central." At present Pan
is in Hongkong engaged in making arrangements with Chen
Ming Chu and others of the Anti-Chiang Clique for the
purpose of unifying the Anti-Chiang battle line. If
you want to communicate with him through letter or
telegram, you may request TOONG WEI JIEN (See item I) to
ask his younger brother to dispatch the message for you.
Among those who have connections with Pan, is one
Nyi Poh(倪樸), who also came from "Central" and is
now residing in South China.
(6) TSUI CHING DAUNG (朱錦堂), former clerk of the Hopei
Provincial Committee and former clerk of the National
Mutual Aid Society. At the beginning he was a coal
miner. He is very honest and reliable, and has consider-
able experience.

（批：Can he be traced?）
（批：This indicates that "Central" is not in Shanghai. MK）
（批：Central seems to mean Moscow.）

15美元用于救济处于困境中的华汉（Hwa Han）同志家属。7月份应付的40美元尚未支付。
如果宣传书记（?童博士）与文化联盟的联系中断，你可以找曹兄来整顿局面。他住在兆丰路（Chaoufoong Road）近约克路（Yochow Road）的麦赫斯特中学职员宿舍240室。每周三和周五上午8点至9点他在那里。见他时，请出示我写的附信作为介绍。
(5) 潘汉年（PAN HAN NYI），化名小开（SIAU KAI）。
他从“中央”来到上海，目的是（1）亲自与“毛子”（?外国人）讨论红军的发展，以及（2）为“中央”在“白区”准备一个新的地址，如香港等。然而，他的计划已被敌人发现，据推测是由于从“中央”抵达上海的同志被捕并随后向国民党投降所致。目前潘在香港，正与陈铭枢及其他反蒋派系人士进行安排，旨在统一反蒋战线。如果你想通过信件或电报与他联系，可以请求童伟坚（TOONG WEI JIEN）（见第一项）让他弟弟为你发送消息。
在与潘有联系的人中，有一位倪樸（Nyi Poh），他也来自“中央”，现居华南。
(6) 朱锦堂（TSUI CHING DAUNG），前河北省委干事及前全国互济会干事。起初他是一名煤矿工人。他非常诚实可靠，且有相当丰富的经验。

（批：能追踪到他吗？）
（批：这表明“中央”不在上海。MK）
（批：中央似乎指莫斯科。）

He now manages a shop in Swatow and a firm in
Hongkong - strictly confidential - which purchase
large quantities of medicines and radio sets for
use in the Old Soviet District and remit monies.
As he has been in Swatow for a long time, a number
of renegrades know that he is there. I therefore
request you to find a reliable "schoolmate" (? comrade),
who should be well versed in commerce, to take his
place and then send him to Moscow immediately.
Although he is a veteran of the executive staff, he
has never been abroad.

（批：Please verify all this by inquiries at the hotel. MA）

He will come to Shanghai on July 15 and will
stay in either the Dah Chung (大中) or the Dah Woo
(大沪) Hotel, Av. Edward VII, registering himself
as Tsui Yao Ding(朱耀庭). Please go to see him
in the evening of 15th or 16th with a chit addressed
to "Brother Faung(舫兄)"! Don't be too late
or he may suspect that I have been arrested and may
then return to South China.

(7) LAO NYI (老倪)
He is a reliable comrade well versed in commerce.
He has worked in Hongkong and is in touch with Tsui
Ching Daung (Item 6). Not long ago, he was called
to Shanghai by Nyi Poh(Item 5), who has connections
with Siau Kai (Item 5), for assistance. However, he
was shadowed by enemies upon arrival in Shanghai and
consequently he has temporarily isolated himself
from this organization. He will be able to find us
through Tsui Ching Daung.

（批：Is this place located. If so it should be watched. MA）

(8) SAN TAI SUNDRY GOODS SHOP (三泰雜貨店), Ward Road, corner
of Dalny Road. This shop was established not long ago
and an additional capital of $1,200 was recently put in.
pages.zh:
-6-

他现在在汕头经营一家商店，并在香港经营一家公司——严格保密——该公司购买大量药品和收音机供老苏区使用，并汇款。
由于他在汕头待了很长时间，许多叛徒知道他在那里。因此，我请求你找一位可靠的“同学”（?同志），此人应精通商业，来接替他的位置，然后立即送他去莫斯科。
虽然他是一名资深的执行人员，但他从未出过国。

（批：请通过在旅馆查询来核实所有这些情况。MA）

他将于7月15日抵达上海，并将入住爱多亚路（Av. Edward VII）的大中（Dah Chung）或大沪（Dah Woo）旅馆，登记名为朱耀庭（Tsui Yao Ding）。请在15日或16日晚上带着写给“舫兄”（Brother Faung）的便条去见他！不要太晚，否则他可能会怀疑我被捕了，进而返回华南。

(7) 老倪（LAO NYI）
他是一位精通商业的可靠同志。他在香港工作过，并与朱锦堂（第6项）保持联系。不久前，他被与“小开”（第5项）有联系的倪樸（第5项）召到上海协助工作。然而，他抵达上海后遭到敌人监视，因此暂时与本组织断绝了联系。他将能通过朱锦堂找到我们。

（批：这个地方定位了吗？如果是，应该进行监视。MA）

(8) 三泰杂货店（SAN TAI SUNDRY GOODS SHOP），华德路（Ward Road）与大连路（Dalny Road）转角。这家店是不久前成立的，最近又投入了1200美元的追加资本。

(9) The following connections I have handed over to brother
Tsang here:-
(a) Zau (赵), Chief of the Communications Bureau of Soviet
Districts. He has under him a communications secretary named
Woo (胡) who also controls the Shanghai E.D. Com., and a
communication agent. Apart from his usual duties, Zau
supervises the dispatching of letters and money to the Com-
munist Youth League. Zau also controls one Siau Zung (小隋)
who controls letter-transmitting offices at various places,
which, however, have not yet been utilized. I have given a
secret code book to brother Tsang. These addresses are most
probably known to Tsang Wei Yih (張維一) alias Lau Tah Yah
(老太爺), who has been arrested but has not turned out to be
a provocateur.
Please send immediately the living expenses for the
child of Loo Tung Yen (羅登賢), who has already sacrificed
his life. It is $5 a month to be remitted once in three months.
(b) Interpreter Wong (王), already mentioned.
(c) Doo Ah Pao (杜阿保) who controls the printing and dis-
patching offices, the mother and son named Ling (林); the
Lao Tai Boo (old woman) whose surroundings in Shanghai are
bad. He also dispatches documents to a documents-transmitting
office.

其真实目的是在厨房上方的房间里安置无法找到住所的中央负责同志。经理洪文蔚（Hoong Wen Wei）精通商业，但他仅是一名“同情者”，对“我们学校的内容”（?党组织的具体情况）知之甚少。你去那里时必须说：“我是王。是曾先生让我来的。”
这家店的性质只有我和秦邦宪（Zing Paung Shien）的弟弟小陈（Siao Zung）知道，小陈已前往莫斯科。

请立即寄送已牺牲的罗登贤（Loo Tung Yen）孩子的生活费。每月5美元，每三个月汇一次。
(b) 译员王（Wong），前文已提及。
(c) 杜阿保（Doo Ah Pao），他控制印刷和发送机构，还有姓林（Ling）的母子；以及老太婆（Lao Tai Boo），她在上海的环境不好。他还向一个文件传递站发送文件。

(1) TSANG WEI LING (Item 2) lives at No. 110 Yen Yang
Tsung(涵養), Connaught Road, west of Medhurst
Road. Passwords: "I am sent by Mr. Woo(吳 )."
Tsang has little translation work to do and
so we want him to assist Dr. Toong. These two
men know each other's address.
Tsang has under him one "Carpenter Tsang",
who will proceed to the North-West soon.
(2) The secret radio code between "Shanghai" and
"Central" is made out as follows:-
Take the open code-figure for the first word
of the 1st Section of the International Song --
giving up the repeating sentences at the end -- and
add it to the open code-figure for the first word
of our message. The open code-figure for the
second word of the song is to be added to the open
code-figure of the second word of our message and
so on. When the first Section of the song is
completed, go over it again. The second and third
sections of the Song are not used.
(3) TOONG WEI JIEN (Item 1) has asked a foreign
comrade to get a radio station for "calling and
listening" (??). The result is unknown.

our Brother Tsang went there once. He does not

social relations with us.

in Shanghai. Interpreter Tsang --> Alarm

representative is suspicious in connection with
the raid on the Shanghai Central Bureau last year,

These lists give ample proof of the Communist activities of the 1st, 2nd, 4th and 5th accused.
With regard to the 3rd accused — Lee Chien (李健), close interrogation during the period of remand has failed to shake his story of only having arrived in Shanghai from Nanking on the day of his arrest.
However, he was taken to Gordon Road Station on the 29-7-35, when he was identified by Tsang Yih San (張益三), the 2nd accused in the Gordon Road Communist case, as one named Yih (葉), whom he (Tsang Yih San) had previously known as a Communist. Tsang Yih San could give no further information about the 3rd accused, but it is worthy of note that the 3rd accused obviously recognised Tsang Yih San when confronted with him in the Gordon Road detective office, and he attempted to signal to Tsang by slowly shaking his head, thereby trying to tell Tsang not to identify him.

Tsang Yao Ching ( 曹堯臣 )
Sien Zien Hsien, Shansi
P.S.S. translated xxxxxxx Clerk Chiang

My real name is Tsang Tsu Daung ( 曹佐臣 ), native
of Sien Zien Hsien ( 西泉村, ), Shansi, age 27, male, residing
on 1st floor at No.39 Urga Road. I had been engaged as clerk
to organs, and teacher in primary schools, and had acted as
merchant, etc. before I came here from my wife's home. Here
I became acquainted with a person named Lieu ( 刘 ) (the latter
said himself that he was named Wong 王 ), a member of the
C.P. I do not know whether he is undertaking any work locally;
when I was on my way to here he told me that he would esta-
blish connections for me upon my arrival at Shanghai. After
I had reached Shanghai he came to see me. He is often seen
going to and fro on the streets and it is probable that he
is working as a communication agent. Later I was introduced
by him to another person named Dsung ( 陈 ) and a girl of
about 20 years of age. (At that time he used passwords; he
did not tell me their names). We took lodgings together at
the Grand Hotel for about 20 days during which period I was
asked to find a house as my residence, posing as being en-
gaged in an open profession. Afterwards, I was provided by
them with clothings.

On June 3 I removed from the hotel to No.39 Zung
Tuh Faung ( 功德坊 ) Urga Road, where I lived about half a
month when a man named Woo ( 吴 ) came to live at the same house
and said that he was the responsible person. Several days
after, the girl in question told me to work as an arts
secretary. Woo said that I was asked to assist in the work
pages.zh:
Tsang Yao Ching ( 曹堯臣 )
山西 Sien Zien Hsien
公共租界巡捕房翻译 xxxxxxx 书记员 Chiang

我真名是 Tsang Tsu Daung ( 曹佐臣 )，籍贯山西 Sien Zien Hsien ( 西泉村, )，年龄27岁，男性，居住在乌尔嘎路39号一楼。在从岳母家来到此处之前，我曾受雇于机关担任书记员，在小学任教，并从事过商人等职业。在这里，我结识了一位姓刘 ( 刘 ) 的人（后者自称姓王 ( 王 )），他是共产党成员。我不知道他是否在当地从事任何工作；在我来这里的路上，他告诉我，抵达上海后会为我建立联系。我到达上海后，他来看望我。经常看到他在街上来往，很可能他是一名交通员。后来，他把我介绍给另一位姓陈 ( 陈 ) 的人和一名约20岁的女孩。（当时他使用了口令；他没有告诉我他们的名字）。我们在 Grand Hotel 一起住宿了约20天，在此期间，我被要求找一处房子作为住所，伪装成从事正当职业。之后，他们为我提供了衣物。

6月3日，我从酒店搬至乌尔嘎路 Zung Tuh Faung ( 功德坊 ) 39号，在那里住了约半个月，随后一名姓吴 ( 吴 ) 的男子来同住，并称自己是负责人。几天后，前述女孩让我担任文书秘书。吴说让我协助工作，

pages.en:
- 2 -
because it was too much for him personally to accomplish.
The drafts of articles were made by him and copied down
by me. After having copied them down, I handed them back
to him for printing. He said that I was quite all right as
I could work hard, but that I had a very poor knowledge
of politics. Therefore, I was entrusted in copying work
all the time.
pages.zh:
- 2 -
因为他个人无法完成所有工作。
文章草稿由他起草，由我抄写。抄写完毕后，我交还给他进行印刷。他说我工作努力，表现不错，但我的政治知识非常贫乏。因此，我一直受托从事抄写工作。

The five accused were arraigned before the 2nd Branch
Kiangsu High Court on the 23-7-35, when evidence was heard
and they were remanded sine die for further enquiries.
The 5th accused admitted in open Court that he had
joined the Communist Party two years ago in Shansi, and
that he came to Shanghai recently to open up a provision
store which was to be used as the Headquarters of the
Party in Shanghai.

was temporarily handed over to the S.P.S.B. for enquiries
by D.S.Jones on instructions of Mr. Givens, D.C. Special

carried out on a communist base at 39 Urga Road on July 22, 1935.
At the time of the raid the only occupant of the
room in which the seizure was made was a female, Tsang Yang Sa
(張楊氏). At 7 p.m. the same day her husband, Tsang Yao
Ching (張堯臣), returned to the room and was arrested.
Tsang does not appear to be the author of any of
the documents, but only custodian, in whose possession
incriminating material is left. This accounts for the fact
that nothing was found at the home of Tsang Bei Ling (張培齡),
at 29, Lane 648, Ferry Road.
Tsang Bei Ling is a member of the Committee of the
Central Communications Department of the Chinese Communist
Party, and according to Tsang Yao Ching the documents found
at 39 Urga Road were left there by him.
J. Coyne
D. S. I.
D. C. (Special Branch).

档案编号 RICI
S. 2, 特别分部，
报告
日期：1935年7月29日。
事由：关于1935年7月22日在乌尔嘎路39号查获的第32号文件。
由 D.S.I. Coyne 撰写。转呈者
兹随函附上一份报告的译文，该报告是第32号证物，属于一批类似文件的大宗查获物。这些文件是警方于1935年7月22日凭上海特区法院搜查令，对位于乌尔嘎路39号的共产党据点实施突击搜查时获得的。
搜查时，查获文件的房间内唯一的居住者是一名女性，张杨氏（Tsang Yang Sa）。当晚7时，其丈夫张尧臣（Tsang Yao Ching）回到房间并被捕。
张尧臣似乎并非任何文件的作者，而仅是保管人，罪证材料被留在他手中。这就解释了为何在斐伦路648弄29号张培龄（Tsang Bei Ling）的家中未搜获任何东西。
张培龄是中国共产党中央交通委员会成员，据张尧臣称，在乌尔嘎路39号发现的文件是由他留在那里的。
J. Coyne
副首席督察
副总监（特别分部）。

S. 2, Special Branch,
REPORT
Date July 29, 19 35.
Subject Re. Document No.32 containing reference to the "New
Life Weekly" case.
Made by D.S.I. Coyne. Forwarded by.
On July 22, 1935 the Police raided 39 Urga Road
and seized a quantity of communistic literature and documents.
According to Tsang Yao Ching (張臣), arrested at that
address, the documents were left there by Tsang Bei Ling (張培齡),
a member of the Committee of the Central Communications Depart-
ment of the Chinese Communist Party, who was arrested the
same day after being followed from his home at 29, Lane 648,
Ferry Road.
Among the documents seized was a lengthy report
containing reference to the "New Life Weekly" case, in which
it is stated that a Cultural League is controlled by Dr. Toong
Wei Jien (董維健).
The author of the document states that the League
is engaged in opposing the judgment in the "New Life Weekly"
case, in connection with which a demonstration was held in
the Court. He also comments on his instructions to members
of the League on anti-Japanese and anti-Chiang Kai Shek
activities.
J Coyne
D. S. I.
D. C. (Special Branch).

日期：1935年7月29日。
事由：关于包含提及“新生周刊”案的第32号文件。
由 D.S.I. Coyne 撰写。转呈者。
1935年7月22日，警方突击搜查了乌尔嘎路39号，查获了大量共产主义文学刊物和文件。
据在该地址被捕的张臣（Tsang Yao Ching，原文如此，前文为张尧臣）称，这些文件是由中国共产党中央交通委员会成员张培龄（Tsang Bei Ling）留在那里的。张培龄当天从其斐伦路648弄29号的住所被跟踪后被捕。
在查获的文件中，有一份长篇报告提及“新生周刊”案，其中指出一个文化联盟由董维健博士（Dr. Toong Wei Jien）控制。
该文件的作者指出，该联盟致力于反对“新生周刊”案的判决，并为此在法庭举行了一次示威活动。他还评论了他向联盟成员下达的关于反日和反蒋介石活动的指示。
J Coyne
D. S. I.
副总监（特别分部）。

TRANSLATION OF DOCUMENT IN QUESTION
                        July 11.

Big Brother:-

    I beg to submit the following report on the
persons, monies and documents that have been assigned
to my management:-

                1. Personnel

1) Dr. Tsang Wai Jian(董維健), propaganda secretary.
He has under his control a propaganda clerk named
Pan( 潘 ), a mimeograph printing office, and the Cultural
League which is the principal organ for directing the
cultural movement.

    The Cultural League is at present endeavouring to
extend the movement to oppose the judgment in the case
against the "New Life Weekly." In connection with
this movement, a demonstration was held in the Kiangsu
High Court the day before yesterday while preparations
will be made for assaulting Dr. Wang Ching Wei and
killing Japanese people.

    However, I told the man of the League that, while
pages.zh:

附于本文件的两张便条的译文——

便条 (a)。

亮兄，          7月11日。

    请与持附文件的我的朋友王先生( Wang )安排事宜。

                    （签名）M. C. Chang（英文）。
                             张纯初（Tsang Sung Tsoe）
                             （中文）。

便条 (b)。

芳兄（Faung，音译，原文括号内为“射”，疑为OCR错误或特定代号），          7月15日。

    你致朱汝康先生（Mr. Tsui Zae Keng）的信已收到。因我 somewhat busy（稍忙），特请王先生( Wang )与你安排事宜。

                    （签名）张三福（Tiang San Fah）

涉案文件译文
                        7月11日。

大哥：

    谨就指派我管理的人员、资金和文件提交如下报告：

                1. 人员

1) 董维健博士（Dr. Tsang Wai Jian，姓氏拼音与中文名不符，保留原文拼音及对应中文名），宣传秘书。他手下控制着一名姓潘（Pan）的宣传干事、一个油印印刷所，以及作为指导文化运动主要机构的文化联盟。

    文化联盟目前正努力扩大运动，以反对针对“新生周刊”案的判决。与此运动相关，前天在江苏高等法院举行了一次示威活动，同时正在准备袭击汪精卫博士并杀害日本人。

    然而，我告诉联盟的人，虽然

pages.en:
-2-
attacking Wang we should also storm Chiang Kai Shek's
residence in Shanghai so as to show the Chinese people
that both Chiang and Wang are national traitors. I also
told them that we should not commit the blunder of
killing Japanese people because this would lead to
renewed armed attacks upon China by Japan and would
enable Chiang Kai Shek to accuse us of being the
instigators of Sino-Japanese conflicts. My opinion is
that it will be sufficient for us to hold demonstrations
or "flying" meetings in front of Japanese anti-revolutionary
societies in Shanghai, breaking their window panes,
distributing anti-Japanese pamphlets and shouting slogans.
This struggle is now developing rapidly.
The directorship of the "Tang-Tuan" (Party &
Communist Youth League) in the Cultural League has been
weakened by the recent arrest of a number of its executive
members, while Dr. TOONG, leader of the Cultural League,
is not very much experienced in directing struggles.
Please take this important problem into your consideration
and establish close connections with him so as to
increase our efficiency.
DR. TOONG is also the editor of the "Struggle."
Although formerly he wrote a number of left-inclined
books and articles of a mild nature, he wrote very
little Party literature. It is therefore problematical
that he should be entrusted with the writing of important
articles.
He is honest and reliable and has been in our
Party for nine years. He appears to be more energetic
recently. His surroundings in Shanghai are not
suitable.
Among the persons who have connections with
DR. TOONG, is an American lady, his former schoolmate,
who has come to Shanghai with the intention of publishing
pages.zh:
-2-
攻击汪的同时，我们也应冲击蒋介石在上海的寓所，以便向中国人民显示蒋和汪都是民族叛徒。我还告诉他们，我们不应犯下杀害日本人的错误，因为这将导致日本对中国重新发动武装攻击，并使蒋介石能够指责我们是中日冲突的煽动者。我的意见是，我们只需在上海的日本反革命社团前举行示威或“飞行”集会，打碎他们的窗玻璃，分发反日传单并高呼口号即可。这场斗争目前正在迅速发展。
由于最近逮捕了其多名执行委员，文化联盟中“党团”（党和共青团）的领导力量已被削弱，而文化联盟领导人董博士（DR. TOONG）在指导斗争方面经验不是很丰富。请将此重要问题纳入考虑，并与他建立紧密联系，以提高我们的效率。
董博士也是《斗争》的编辑。虽然以前他写过一些倾向左翼但性质温和的书籍和文章，但他很少撰写党的文献。因此，委托他撰写重要文章是有问题的。
他诚实可靠，已入党九年。他最近显得更有活力。他在上海的环境并不适宜。
在与董博士有关系的人中，有一位美国女士，是他以前的同学，她来上海打算出版

pages.en:
-3-

a left-inclined Anglo-Chinese magazine. It is a pity
that her antecedents and plans are known to our enemies
due to the seizure of her letters at the place of a
responsible comrade, but our enemies do not know that
she is the author of the plans. She came to Shanghai
with the introduction of a very influential person
in the U.S.A. and she has suitable protection. She
still intends to publish a magazine. Please write an
English letter to her, to be sent through DR. TOONG,
requesting her not to take the risk of publishing
the periodical but to collect materials for writing
books on China's revolution. I do not know her name
but you may address her "Dear Friend" and give your
name "William."

DR. TOONG also knows the address of a German
who poses as a Dentist. A quantity of old publications
of the International in Chinese is kept at this
German's place.

In addition, DR. TOONG knows a banker named
TSUNG HAI CHI(章乃器), who sympathises with us and
is concerned with the "Soviet Friendly Society."
TOONG is also on friendly terms with a certain BUNN(邵P)
of the Honan Provincial Government; the former intends
to propagate our anti-Chiang policy through the latter.

Arrested
here on 27/7/35.
Warrant applied
for by P.S.D.

TOONG resides in the front room, 3rd Floor,
No. 20 Jui Tyh Li(瑞德里), Sinsa Road, East of Northurst
Road. Passwords: "Introduced by Mr. Woo(胡)."

---

(2) Interpreter TSANG WUI LING(張林).
Joined (? the Party) in 1927. Honest. Political
knowledge: common.

Ma Hse Yu(毛子) (? meaning foreigner) in Shanghai
is an artist. He simply forwards the translated
documents to Moscow without putting on any comments.
pages.zh:
-3-

一份倾向左翼的中英双语杂志。遗憾的是，由于在一位负责同志处查获了她的信件，她的背景和计划已被敌人知晓，但敌人并不知道她是这些计划的作者。她是在美国一位极具影响力的人物的介绍下来到上海的，并且拥有适当的保护。她仍打算出版一份杂志。请写一封英文信给她，通过董博士转交，要求她不要承担出版期刊的风险，而是收集材料以撰写关于中国革命的书籍。我不知道她的名字，但你可以称呼她“亲爱的朋友”，并署名“威廉”。

董博士也知道一位伪装成牙医的德国人的地址。大量中文版的《国际》旧刊物保存在这个德国人那里。

此外，董博士认识一位名叫章乃器（TSUNG HAI CHI）的银行家，他同情我们，并与“苏俄之友社”有关联。
董还与河南省政府的某位邵P（BUNN，音译）关系友好；前者打算通过后者宣传我们的反蒋政策。

于此地于1935年7月27日
被捕。
由警务处申请
搜查令。

董居住在诺斯赫斯特路以东新闸路瑞德里20号三楼前间。暗号：“胡先生介绍。”

---

(2) 翻译员张林（TSANG WUI LING）。
1927年加入（？党）。诚实。政治知识：普通。

在上海的马子（Ma Hse Yu，？意为外国人）是一位艺术家。他只是将翻译好的文件送往莫斯科，不加任何评论。

pages.en:
-4-
Consequently you must send to "Mao Ts" regularly our
resolutions in Chinese, reports from various provinces,
and publications of the "Central" to be forwarded (to
Moscow). Ask "schoolmate Tsang" (? "schoolmate"
most probably means "comrade") here to send such documents
to Doe Ah Pae(杜阿保), who, in turn, will send them
to the documents office, marked "Home, c/o Tsung Zean"
(坐控钟). You may ask Tsang Wei Ling (張維林) to
translate comparatively important documents, but in
the case of strictly confidential documents, you must
find a very reliable translator anticipating that Tsang
might inadvertently disclose information.
(3) Interpreter WONG ( 王 ).
He is a "sympathiser" whom we engaged this year.
He can translate the "Communist Monthly" into Chinese,
but his work is not done well and has to be rewritten
by the editor of the "Struggle."
The typewriter in Wong's home is our property.
Wong's address and budgets etc. are all known to
"Schoolmate Tsang" here.
(4) ZAW LIANG (曹亮), Candidate Clerk of the Tong-Tuan
(Party and C.Y. League) in the Cultural League.
He is a member of the executive staff of the
masses and is known to the cultural circle as a
"sympathiser." Actually he has joined our Party
but this truth is known to only two or three persons
who have close connections (with him). He has an
open occupation and conducts his activities in an open
manner. Should his Party membership be known
to many persons, he would be compelled to perform his
duties secretly thus reducing considerably his
efficiency. Consequently we must get very reliable
persons to establish connections with him. Give him
$65. per month, of this amount $15. is to be sent to
comrades imprisoned in the gaol in Nanking and the
pages.zh:
-4-
因此，你必须定期将我们的中文决议、各省报告以及“中央”的出版物发送给“毛茨”（Mao Ts，音译），以便转发（至莫斯科）。请此地的“张同学”（？“同学”很可能指“同志”）将这些文件发送给杜阿保（Doe Ah Pae），再由他发送至文件处，标记为“Home, c/o Tsung Zean”（坐控钟，音译）。你可以让张维林（Tsang Wei Ling）翻译比较重要的文件，但在处理绝密文件时，你必须寻找非常可靠的翻译员，以防张可能无意中泄露信息。
(3) 翻译员王（WONG）。
他是我们今年雇用的一名“同情者”。他能将《共产主义月刊》翻译成中文，但工作做得不好，必须由《斗争》的编辑重写。
王家中的打字机是我们的财产。
王的地址和预算等均为此地的“张同学”所知。
(4) 曹亮（ZAW LIANG），文化联盟中党团（党和共青团）的候选干事。
他是群众执行 staff 的成员，在文化界以“同情者”闻名。实际上他已加入我们党，但这一真相只有两三个与他有密切关系的人知道。他有公开的职业，并以公开方式进行活动。如果他的党员身份被许多人知晓，他将被迫秘密履行职责，从而大大降低其效率。因此，我们必须派遣非常可靠的人与他建立联系。每月给他65美元，其中15美元要寄给关押在南京监狱的同志，以及

pages.en:
-5-
remaining $15. is for the family of Comrade Hwa Han
(華漢) who is in distress. The $40. due in July
has not yet been paid.
In case the connections between the Propaganda
Secretary (? Dr. Toong) and the Cultural League are
broken, you may find brother ZAU to set things in
order. He lives in Room 240, staff dormitory of
the Medhurst Middle School, Chaowfoeng Road, near
Yochow Road. He will be there between 8 a.m. and
9 a.m. every Wednesday and Friday. When meeting him,
please produce the attached note written by me as an
introduction.
(5) PAN HAN NYI(潘漢年) alias SIAU KAI (小開).
He came to Shanghai from "Central" for the purpose
of (1) discussing with "Mao Ts" (? foreigner) personally
about the development of Red armies, and (2) preparing
a new address, such as Hongkong etc., for the "Central"
in "White" territory. His plans, however, have been
discovered by enemies presumably due to the arrest and
subsequent surrender to the Kuomintang of comrades
arrived in Shanghai from "Central." At present Pan
is in Nangking engaged in making arrangements with Chen
Ming Chu and others of the Anti-Chiang Clique for the
purpose of unifying the Anti-Chiang battle line. If
you want to communicate with him through letter or
telegram, you may request TOONG WEI JEN (See item 2) to
ask his younger brother to dispatch the message for you.
Among those who have connections with Pan, is one
Hsi Shih(徽樸), who also came from "Central" and is
now residing in South China.
(6) SHU CHING TANG (朱錦堂), former clerk of the Hopei
Provincial Committee and former clerk of the National
Mutual Aid Society. At the beginning he was a coal
miner. He is very honest and reliable, and has consider-
able experience.
pages.zh:
-5-
余款15美元用于接济处于困境中的华汉（Hwa Han）同志家属。7月份应付的40美元尚未支付。
如果宣传书记（？童博士）与文化同盟之间的联系中断，你可以找ZAU兄弟来整顿局面。他住在兆丰路（Chaowfoeng Road）近约克路（Yochow Road）的麦赫斯特中学（Medhurst Middle School）职员宿舍240室。每周三和周五上午8点至9点他都在那里。与他见面时，请出示我附上的介绍信。
(5) 潘汉年（PAN HAN NYI），化名小开（SIAU KAI）。
他从“中央”来到上海，目的是（1）亲自与“毛茨”（Mao Ts，？外国人）讨论红军的发展问题，以及（2）为“中央”在“白区”准备一个新的地址，如香港等。然而，他的计划已被敌人察觉，这大概是由于从“中央”抵达上海的同志被捕并随后向国民党投诚所致。目前潘正在南京，与陈铭枢及其他反蒋派人士进行安排，旨在统一反蒋战线。如果你想通过信件或电报与他联系，可以请求童维坚（TOONG WEI JEN，见第2项）让其弟弟为你发送消息。
与潘有联系的人中有一位徽樸（Hsi Shih，音译），他也来自“中央”，现居华南地区。
(6) 朱锦堂（SHU CHING TANG），前河北省委办事员，前全国互济会办事员。他起初是一名煤矿工人。他非常诚实可靠，且经验丰富。

pages.en:
-6-

He now manages a shop in Swatow and a firm in
Hongkong - strictly confidential - which purchase
large quantities of medicines and radio sets for
use in the Old Soviet District and remit monies.
As he has been in Swatow for a long time, a number
of renegades know that he is there. I therefore
request you to find a reliable "schoolmate" (? comrade),
who should be well versed in commerce, to take his
place and then send him to Moscow immediately.
Although he is a veteran of the executive staff, he
has never been abroad.

He will come to Shanghai on July 15 and will
stay in either the Dah Chung (大中) or the Dah Woo
(大沪) Hotel, Av. Edward VII, registering himself
as Tsui Yao Ding(朱耀庭). Please go to see him
in the evening of 15th or 16th with a chit addressed
to "Brother Fung(舫兄)"! Don't be too late
or he may suspect that I have been arrested and may
then return to South China.

(7) LAO NI (老倪)

He is a reliable comrade well versed in commerce.
He has worked in Hongkong and is in touch with Tsui
Ching Bang (Item 6). Not long ago, he was called
to Shanghai by Nyi Pah(Item 5), who has connections
with Siau Kai (Item 5), for assistance. However, he
was shadowed by enemies upon arrival in Shanghai and
consequently he has temporarily isolated himself
from this organisation. He will be able to find us
through Tsui Ching Bang.

(8) SAN TAI GENERAL GOODS SHOP (三泰百貨店), Ward Road, corner
of Dalny Road. This shop was established not long ago
and an additional capital of $1,200 was recently put in.
pages.zh:
-6-

他目前在汕头经营一家商店，并在香港经营一家公司——严格保密——这两处机构为老苏区大量采购药品和无线电设备，并汇款。由于他在汕头待了很长时间，许多叛徒都知道他在那里。因此，我请求你找一位可靠的“同学”（？同志），此人应精通商业，去接替他的位置，然后立即送他去莫斯科。虽然他是一位资深的执行人员，但他从未出过国。

他将于7月15日抵达上海，入住爱多亚路（Av. Edward VII）的大中（Dah Chung）酒店或大沪（Dah Woo）酒店，登记姓名为朱耀庭（Tsui Yao Ding）。请在15日或16日晚上带着写给“舫兄”的字条去见他！不要太晚，否则他可能会怀疑我已被捕，从而返回华南。

(7) 老倪（LAO NI）

他是一位精通商业的可靠同志。他曾在香港工作，并与朱锦堂（第6项）保持联系。不久前，他被倪巴（Nyi Pah，第5项）召到上海协助工作，倪巴与小开（第5项）有联系。然而，他抵达上海后遭到敌人监视，因此暂时与本组织断绝了联系。他将能通过朱锦堂找到我们。

(8) 三泰百货店（SAN TAI GENERAL GOODS SHOP），位于华德路（Ward Road）与大连路（Dalny Road）转角。该店是不久前成立的，最近又追加了1,200美元资本。

pages.en:
- 7 -

the real object is to accommodate in the room over kitchen respon-
sible comrades of the Central who cannot find a place for
residing. The manager Hoong Wen Wei (洪文蔚) is well versed
in commerce but he is merely a "sympathizer," and doesn't
know much about the "contents of our school". (? the parti-
culars of the Party organization). When you go there you
have to say "I am Wong. It is Mr. Tsang who told me to come."
The nature of this shop is only known to me and Siau Zung
(小陈), who is the younger brother of Sing Paung Shien
(秦邦憲) and who has left for Moscow.
(9) The following connections I have handed over to brother
Tsang here:-
(a) Zan (坚), Chief of the Communications Bureau of Soviet
Districts. He has under him a communications secretary named
Woo (胡) who also controls the Shanghai E.D. Com., and a
communication agent. Apart from his usual duties, Zan
supervises the dispatching of letters and money to the Com-
munist Youth League. Zan also controls one Siau Zung (小陈)
who controls letter-transmitting offices at various places,
which, however, have not yet been utilized. I have given a
secret code book to brother Tsang. These addresses are most
probably known to Tsang Wei Yih (张唯一) alias Lau Tah Yah
(老太爺), who has been arrested but has not turned out to be
a provocateur.
Please send immediately the living expenses for the
child of Loo Tung Yen (羅登賢), who has already sacrificed
his life. It is $5 a month to be remitted once in three months.
(b) Interpreter Wong (王), already mentioned.
(c) Boo Ah Pao (杜阿保) who controls the printing and dis-
patching offices, the mother and son named Ling (林); the
Lao Tai Boo (old woman) whose surroundings in Shanghai are
bad. He also dispatches documents to a documents-transmitting
office.
pages.zh:
- 7 -

其真实目的是在厨房上方的房间里安置无法找到居住地的中央负责同志。经理洪文蔚（Hoong Wen Wei）精通商业，但他仅仅是一名“同情者”，对“我们学校的内容”（？党组织的具体情况）知之甚少。你去那里时必须说：“我是王，是曾先生让我来的。”这家店的性质只有我和小陈（Siau Zung，音译）知道，小陈是秦邦宪（Sing Paung Shien）的弟弟，已前往莫斯科。
(9) 以下关系我已在此移交给曾兄弟：-
(a) 坚（Zan，音译），苏区交通局局长。他手下有一名通讯秘书胡（Woo，音译），该人也控制着上海东区委员会，还有一名交通员。除了日常职责外，坚还监督向共产主义青年团发送信件和款项。坚还控制着一名小陈（Siau Zung，音译），此人控制着各地的信件传递站，但这些站点尚未投入使用。我已将一本密码本交给曾兄弟。这些地址很可能张唯一（Tsang Wei Yih），又名老太爷（Lau Tah Yah，音译）也知道，他已被捕，但并未成为挑衅者（即未叛变）。
请立即汇寄已牺牲的罗登贤（Loo Tung Yen）孩子的生活费。每月5美元，每三个月汇寄一次。
(b) 翻译王（Wong，音译），前文已提及。
(c) 杜阿保（Boo Ah Pao，音译），控制印刷和分发机构，还有林（Ling，音译）姓母子；以及老太婆（Lao Tai Boo，音译），她在上海的环境不好。他还向文件传递站发送文件。

pages.en:
- 8 -

(d) Chief of the Alarm Station. He has under him an execu-
tive secretary named Tsang Tsung Doh (曾振鐸) who dispatches
letters to the National Labour Federation.
(e) There many minor problems which will be related to
you by Brother Tsang in person.

11. Financial Matters
Statements of accounts and cash on hand
$1,258.85 - given to brother Tsang in person.
$2,200.00 - taken from me by Brother Tsang who will
report as to how the sum was spent.
$400. - spent by me as follows:-
Allowance for my two children......$120/
Cantonese Amah's two children......$144.
Passage for Old Woman whom I sent $ 15.
for to live in the office as I am
going to travel.
My expenses in travelling $ 50.
One fountain $15.
Clothing and expenses in Shai. $ 36.
Expenses in connection with the $ 20.
death of my mother.
Total: $400.00

A sum of $500 can be taken from the balance for the dis-
posal of Brother Tsang while the remainder can be left at
some other suitable place because nobody will look after
the house when he is away.

III Documents.
(1) One parcel of documents needs be sent to the archive
for safe keeping.
(2) One parcel is to be sent to the Manchurian Communist
Youth League through the courier from Manchuria.
pages.zh:
- 8 -

(d) 警报站站长。他手下有一名执行秘书曾振铎（Tsang Tsung Doh，音译），负责向全国劳工联合会发送信件。
(e) 还有许多小问题，将由曾兄弟当面告诉你。

11. 财务事项
账目报表及手头现金
1,258.85美元 - 当面交给曾兄弟。
2,200.00美元 - 由曾兄弟从我处取走，他将报告这笔款项的使用情况。
400美元 - 由我支出如下：-
我的两个孩子的津贴......120美元/
广东保姆的两个孩子......144美元。
送我同住办公室的老妇人的路费 15美元。
因我将出行。
我的旅费 50美元。
一支钢笔 15美元。
在上海的衣物及费用 36美元。
与我母亲去世相关的费用 20美元。
总计：400.00美元

可以从余额中取出500美元供曾兄弟支配，其余部分可以留在其他合适的地方，因为他离开后无人照看房子。

III 文件。
(1) 一包文件需送往档案室妥善保管。
(2) 一包文件需通过满洲来的信使送往满洲共产主义青年团。

pages.en:
- 9 -

(3) One parcel was received from Moscow. Please pick
out those documents that need be printed, and give
them to the oil printing office through Dr. Toong
Wei Jien.

(4) The other documents have been obtained by me for
reference. If you don't want to read them, please
write a letter to the archive to take them away
for safekeeping.
Route:- Toong Wei Jien --> Oil Printing Office -->
office of the archive for making arrangements--
Archive

Sung Woo (聖五), July 11.

Supplement

7) Liang Ming Dah (梁明達), real name Tseng Laung
Poo (張浪波), former Chief of the Communications
Bureau. Has been permitted to proceed to
Moscow to resume his studies. Please pay
attention to this.
pages.zh:
- 9 -

(3) 收到来自莫斯科的一包文件。请挑出需要打印的文件，并通过童维坚（Toong Wei Jien）博士交给油印室。

(4) 其他文件是我获取供参考用的。如果你不想阅读，请写信给档案室将其取走保管。
路线：- 童维坚 --> 油印室 --> 档案室办公室进行安排 -- 档案室

圣五（Sung Woo，音译），7月11日。

补充

7) 梁明达（Liang Ming Dah），真名张浪波（Tseng Laung Poo，音译），前交通局局长。已获准前往莫斯科继续学业。请注意此事。

pages.en:
-10-
(1) TSANG WEI LING (Item 2) lives at No. 110 Yen Yang
Tsung(涵養), Connaught Road, west of Medhurst
Road. Passwords: "I am sent by Mr. Woo(吳)."
Tsang has little translation work to do and
so we want him to assist Dr. Toong. These two
men know each other's address.
Tsang has under him one "Carpenter Tsang",
who will proceed to the North-West soon.
(2) The secret radio code between "Shanghai" and
"Central" is made out as follows:-
Take the open code-figure for the first word
of the 1st Section of the International Song --
giving up the repeating sentences at the end -- and
add it to the open code-figure for the first word
of our message. The open code-figure for the
second word of the song is to be added to the open
code-figure of the second word of our message and
so on. When the first Section of the song is
completed, go over it again. The second and third
sections of the Song are not used.
(3) TOONG WEI JIN (Item 1) has asked a foreign
comrade to get a radio station for "calling and
listening" (??). The result is unknown.
(4) As regards the San Tai Embry Goods Shop (item 8)
our Brother Tsang went there once. He does not
know the nature of the shop, neither that the shop
belongs to us. He only knows that the shop has
social relations with us.
(5) The representative of "Malayan Central" has arrived
in Shanghai. Interpreter Tsang -->Alarm
Secretary -->Wong Ling(黃零) -->Representative
of Malayan Communist Party. The Malayan
representative is suspicious in connection with
the raid on the Shanghai Central Bureau last year.
pages.zh:
-10-
(1) 曾维灵（TSANG WEI LING，第2项）住在康纳特路（Connaught Road）、麦赫斯特路以西的涵养（Yen Yang Tsung，音译）110号。口令：“我是吴先生派来的。”
曾的翻译工作很少，所以我们希望他协助童博士。这两人知道彼此的地址。
曾手下有一名“木匠曾”，他即将前往西北。
(2) “上海”与“中央”之间的秘密无线电密码编制如下：-
取《国际歌》第一段第一个字的公开码数——省略末尾的重复句子——加上我们消息中第一个字的公开码数。歌曲第二个字的公开码数加上我们消息中第二个字的公开码数，依此类推。当歌曲的第一段完成后，再从头开始。歌曲的第二段和第三段不使用。
(3) 童维坚（TOONG WEI JIN，第1项）已请一位外国同志为“呼叫和监听”（？？）获取一个无线电台。结果未知。
(4) 关于三泰胚胎商品店（San Tai Embry Goods Shop，第8项，原文如此，疑为General之误），我们的曾兄弟去过一次。他不知道这家店的性质，也不知道这家店属于我们。他只知道这家店与我们有社会关系。
(5) “马来亚中央”的代表已抵达上海。翻译曾 --> 警报秘书 --> 黄零（Wong Ling，音译） --> 马来亚共产党代表。马来亚代表与去年上海中央局遭突袭一事有关联，令人怀疑。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Assistance to Chinese Authorities in executing three search warrants and warrants of arrest for Communists.

At 11.30 a.m. on the 22-7-35, a telephone message was received by the Senior Detective at Hongkew from D.I.Everest of the Special Branch to the effect that a number of warrants had been applied for on behalf of the S.P.S.B. forthe arrest of Communists and searching of certain premises for Communistic literature.

At 12.45 p.m. the same day, C.P.C. 1575 came to the Station together with a Chinese male and female (the 1st and 2nd accused) named Li Tsa Ming ( 李澤民 ), age 30, Shantung, Unemployed schoolteacher, and Ling Kwei Tsung ( 林桂貞 ), age 23, Hupeh, single female, whom he arrested on Range Road near North Kiangse Road at the request of detective No. 419 of the S.P.S.B., who stated that they were wanted by the Chinese Authorities for Communistic activities.

Questioned by detectives, these two accused both stated that they were strangers to Shanghai, having only arrived from Shantung on the same morning - 22/7/35. Questioned about their luggage they said that they did not bring any with them, and that they were looking for rooms when arrested, and they both denied being Communists.

At 2.30 p.m. on the 22-7-35, D.S. Sansom, D.S. Makaroff, C.D.S. 48 and Clerk Kau of the Special Branch

协助中国当局执行三份搜查令及针对共产党人的逮捕令。

1935年7月22日上午11时30分，虹口捕房的高级侦探接到政治部侦探长 Everest 的电话留言，称代表上海特别市警察局（S.P.S.B.）申请了多份逮捕共产党人及搜查某些处所以查获共产主义文献的令状。

同日下午12时45分，中国巡捕 1575 号与一男一女两名华人（第一和第二被告）来到捕房，男子名为 Li Tsa Ming ( 李澤民 )，30岁，山东籍，失业教师，女子名为 Ling Kwei Tsung ( 林桂貞 )，23岁，湖北籍，未婚女性。他是应上海特别市警察局 419 号侦探的要求，在江西路北路附近的兰路（Range Road）将二人逮捕的。该侦探称，中国当局因二人的共产主义活动而通缉他们。

经侦探讯问，这两名被告均称自己是上海的陌生人，仅于当天上午——1935年7月22日——从山东抵达。问及行李时，他们称未携带任何行李，被捕时正在寻找房间，且两人都否认是共产党人。

Li Tsa Ming (李澤民) age 30.
Shantung. D.S. Sansom.
Hongkew Stn. 22/7/35. Clerk S. Y. Wong.

My name is Li Tsa Ming, age 30, native of Shantung, an unemployed school teacher, residing at No.V9, Lane 426 North Kiangse Road.

I came to Shanghai from Chinan (濟南) Shantung on June 29, 1935 and went to reside at the aforementioned address. I came here on the advice of Wong Kwei Ming (王桂明) who promised me employment in a school.

I do not know where this friend resides; he met me on this a railway station on my arrival - I do not know which station or where it is located, and on the second occasion he visited me at my home. All the literature found at my residence was brought there by Wong Kwei Ming, native of Shantung, who instructed me to take care of it. All the furniture of the room also belongs to Wong. All the suit cases etc. belong to me. I brought to Shanghai $120.00 with me, which I had borrowed.

I graduated at the Te Yoch Middle School (德育中学) in An Chow Hsien (安邱縣) Shantung 9 years ago, then joined the army. On the downfall of Chang Tsung Chang (1927) I left the army and became a school teacher in the Wang Kwan Teng Primary School in Chi Hsien An Tseng (齊河晏城) Shantung, remaining there for about 2 years. Since then I have been unemployed and have lived on a bequest of $1,000.00 from my father. On coming to Shanghai I failed to obtain the employment promised me by Wong.

In March 1935, I began to cohabit with Ling Kuei Tsung (林桂貞) who to-day was arrested with me. Neither of us read any of the literature found at my home, but we knew that it was communistic in character.
pages.zh:
Li Tsa Ming (李澤民)，30岁。
山东籍。Sansom 侦探长。
虹口捕房。1935年7月22日。书记员 S. Y. Wong。

我叫 Li Tsa Ming，30岁，山东籍，失业教师，居住于江西路北路426弄V9号。

我于1935年6月29日从山东济南 (濟南) 来到上海，并居住于上述地址。我是听从 Wong Kwei Ming (王桂明) 的建议来此的，他答应给我在学校安排工作。

我不知道这位朋友住在哪里；我抵达时他在火车站接的我——我不知道是哪个车站，也不知道它位于何处，第二次他是在我家拜访我的。在我住所发现的所有文献都是由山东籍的 Wong Kwei Ming 带来的，他嘱咐我妥善保管。房间内的所有家具也属于 Wong。所有手提箱等物品属于我。我来上海时带了借来的120.00元。

我9年前毕业于山东安邱縣 (安邱縣) 的德育中学 ( Te Yoch Middle School )，随后参军。在张宗昌 ( Chang Tsung Chang ) 倒台（1927年）后，我离开了军队，成为山东齐河晏城 ( Chi Hsien An Tseng ) 王官屯小学 ( Wang Kwan Teng Primary School ) 的教师，在那里待了约2年。此后我一直失业，靠父亲遗留的1,000.00元遗产生活。来到上海后，我未能获得 Wong 承诺的工作。

1935年3月，我开始与 Ling Kuei Tsung (林桂貞) 同居，她今天与我一同被捕。我们都没有阅读在我家发现的任何文献，但我们知道其具有共产主义性质。

Ling Kwei Tsung, age 23.
Ichang, Hupeh. D.S. Sansom.
Hongkew Stn. 22/7/55. Clerk S. Y. Wong.

My name is Ling Kwei Tsung (林桂貞) age 23, native of
Ichang, Hupeh, residing with Mr Li Tse Ming (李澤民) at V9,
Lane 426 N. Kiangsi Road.

I have never attended school and am totally illiterate. We
came to Shanghai about a month ago because a friend, a Northerner
name unknown had promised Li some kind of a job. On our arrival
here this friend met us at the North Railway Station and took
us to V.9, Lane 426 North Kiangsi Road. I don't know where he
lives. Altogether he has visited us on about 6 occasions, sometimes
bringing with him parcels, the contents of which I was not
divulged to me. Li has been unemployed ever since I have known
him, and has lived on money borrowed from some friends. I was
not aware that communistic literature was kept at my home.

Ling Kwei Tsung，23岁。
湖北宜昌。Sansom 侦探长。
虹口捕房。1955年7月22日。书记员 S. Y. Wong。

我叫 Ling Kwei Tsung (林桂貞)，23岁，湖北宜昌人，与 Li Tse Ming (李澤民) 同住于江西路北路426弄V.9号。

我从未上过学，完全是文盲。我们大约一个月前来到上海，因为一位朋友（北方人，姓名不详）答应给 Li 安排某种工作。我们抵达这里时，这位朋友在北火车站接了我们，并将我们带到江西路北路426弄V.9号。我不知道他住在哪里。他总共来看望过我们约6次，有时带来包裹，但我并未被告知包裹内的内容。自从我认识 Li 以来，他一直失业，靠向一些朋友借钱生活。我不知道家里藏有共产主义文献。

Lee Chien (    )
Ichang, Hupei                                D.S. Makaroff
Hongkew Stn.            22/7/35              Clerk Chao Shih-chow.

My name is Lee Chien, 24 years of age, native of
Ichang, Hupei. I was residing in Nanking, at the friend's
house just opposite of the Central University. My friend's
name is Chang Yue (    ), formerly of Kuomintang Hdqrs, Nan-
king, who is at present at Szechuan, attached to Communist
Suppression Army. I never went to any school, but studied at
home. At the age of 18 I left Hupei and followed the 20th Army
commanded by General Yang Sun to Wanhsien, Szechuan, being
engaged as a clerk. Upon arrival in Szechuan, the army was
disbanded, and then I proceeded to Taienshow (    ), Szechuan,
with the object of locating my friend Lee Sz Liang (    ),
who was attached to the "Frontier Defense Army" there. I located
him and through his influence I secured a position of a clerk
in the same army. For the next 3 years I remained on this post,
when the army was disbanded, and then I went to Chungking, where
I established a cigarette and money exchange shop out of my
savings. This shop I kept for about 2 years when I was forced
to close it down on account of slack business. Then I went to
Hankow to see my friend, one Lee Vee Ying, but I was unable to
find him there, so I proceeded to Nanking. Whilst in Nanking
(    )
I met my friend Liao Chuen Tsing, who is working in the Kuomin-
tang Headquarters, Nanking and who presented me to Chang Yue,
his friend, where I was residing since.

On 22/7/35 I came to Shanghai from Nanking by train
at 10.30 a.m. with a view to locate one San Ting (    ), my
friend, who was supposed to be residing at Dah Vee Hotel, Avenue
Edward VII. However, being not familiar with Shanghai, I was

李健 (    )
湖北宜昌                                D.S. Makaroff
虹口捕房            1935年7月22日              书记员赵世周。

我叫李健，24岁，籍贯湖北宜昌。我此前居住在南京，住在中央大学对面的一位朋友家中。我的朋友名叫张岳 (    )，原任职于南京国民党总部，现隶属于四川的“剿共”军。我从未上过学，只是在家自学。18岁时，我离开湖北，跟随杨森将军指挥的第20军前往四川万县，受聘为书记员。抵达四川后，该部队解散，随后我前往四川泰恩秀 (    )（音译），目的是寻找我的朋友李士良 (    )（音译），他当时隶属于那里的“边防军”。我找到了他，并通过他的关系在同一支军队中谋得了一份书记员的职位。在此职位上待了3年后，部队解散，我便去了重庆，用积蓄开了一家香烟和兑换店。这家店我经营了约2年，后因生意清淡被迫关闭。随后我去汉口看望我的朋友李维英 (    )（音译），但未能找到他，于是我便前往南京。在南京期间 (    )
我遇到了我的朋友廖全清 (    )（音译），他在南京国民党总部工作，并将我介绍给他的朋友张岳，此后我便一直住在那里。

1935年7月22日，我乘火车于上午10时30分从南京来到上海，目的是寻找一位名叫三丁 (    )（音译）的朋友，据说他住在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）的大伟旅馆（Dah Vee Hotel）。然而，由于我对上海不熟悉，我

unable to find Dah Woo Hotel, and whilst I was wandering about
on Woosung Road near Tiendong Road at about 2 p.m. I was
arrested by two unknown Chinese who turned me over to a
Chinese Policeman, who brought me to the Station.

I visited Shanghai previously, in March 1935, when
I had stayed here for 10 days with my friend Chang Shih Tsang
(        ), a student of the Great China University at that time.
We resided in the students dormitory by the side of the
university.

I never had interest in any political voice neither
I am connected with any communists.

This statement is true.
pages.zh:
- 2 -
无法找到大吴旅馆（Dah Woo Hotel），下午2点左右，当我在提篮桥路（Tiendong Road）附近的吴淞路上徘徊时，被两名不知名的中国人逮捕，他们将我移交给一名中国警察，后者将我带到了捕房。

我之前曾于1935年3月访问过上海，当时我和我的朋友张世藏 (        )（音译）在这里住了10天，他是当时大夏大学的学生。我们住在大学旁边的学生宿舍里。

我对任何政治言论都不感兴趣，也与任何共产党人没有联系。

此陈述属实。

pages.en:
45 acus

張楊氏
Tsang Yang Sz, age 20.
Hupeh. D.S. Sansom.
Hongkew Stn. 22/7/35. Clerk Kao Yen-keng.

My name is Tsang Yang Sz, age 20, native of Hupeh, residing
59 Urga Road.
I came to Shanghai from Hupeh two months ago, accompanied
by my husband Tsang Yan Zung (張耀臣), a grocer.
I married about two years ago, but know very little of
my husband's private affairs. Up to the time we came to Shanghai
we had a grocery business at the Loh Tien Hsien (羅田縣) Hupeh.
Our purpose in coming here is to act as a purchasing agency
for the business we were connected with in Hupeh.
About 2 month ago a friend of my husband's named Woo (胡)
came to stay with us, bringing with him several trunks and cases
containing books and money etc. He left for an unknown destina-
tion about a fortnight ago, leaving his belongings behind. We
were asked to take care of these belongings until such time as
the owner returned.
My husband left the house this morning at 7 o'clock to
visit his sister in Nanking. He is expected to return on July
24, 1935.
pages.zh:
45 被告

张杨氏
Tsang Yang Sz，20岁。
湖北。D.S. Sansom。
虹口捕房 1935年7月22日。书记员高延庚。

我叫张杨氏，20岁，籍贯湖北，居住于乌尔嘎路（Urga Road）59号。
两个月前，我由丈夫张耀臣（Tsang Yan Zung，职业为杂货商）陪同，从湖北来到上海。
我大约在两年前结婚，但对丈夫的私事知之甚少。在我们来上海之前，我们在湖北罗田县经营一家杂货店。我们来此的目的是作为我们在湖北所从事业务的采购代理。
大约两个月前，我丈夫的一位姓胡（Woo）的朋友来与我们同住，带来了几个装有书籍和金钱等物品的皮箱和箱子。大约两周前，他前往一个未知的目的地，将物品留了下来。我们要我们代为保管这些物品，直到物主回来。
我丈夫今天早上7点离家去南京看望他的姐姐。预计他将于1935年7月24日返回。

pages.en:
Ling Kwei Tsung. age 23.
Ichang, Hupeh. D.S. Sansom.
Hongkew Stn. 22/7/35. Clerk S. Y. Wong.

My name is Ling Kwei Tsung (林桂貞) age 23, native of
Ichang, Hupeh, residing with my Li Tsa Ming (李澤民) at V9,
Lane 436 N. Kiangsi Road.

I have never attended school and am totally illiterate. We
came to Shanghai about a month ago because a friend, a Northerner
name unknown had promised Li some kind of a job. On our arrival
here this friend met us at the North Railway Station and took
us to V.9, Lane 436 North Kiangsi Road. I don't know where he
lives. Altogether he has visited us on about 6 occasions, sometimes
bringing with him parcels, the contents of which I was not
divulged to me. Li has been unemployed ever since I have known
him, and has lived on money borrowed from some friends. I was
not aware that communistic literature was kept at my home.
pages.zh:
林桂贞，23岁。
湖北宜昌。D.S. Sansom。
虹口捕房 1935年7月22日。书记员 S. Y. Wong。

我叫林桂贞（Ling Kwei Tsung），23岁，籍贯湖北宜昌，与李泽民（Li Tsa Ming）同住在北江西路436弄V9号。

我从未上过学，完全是文盲。我们大约一个月前来到上海，因为一位朋友（北方人，姓名不详）答应给李安排某种工作。当我们到达这里时，这位朋友在北火车站接了我们，并带我们到北江西路436弄V9号。我不知道他住在哪里。他总共来看望过我们约6次，有时带来包裹，但我并未被告知包裹内的内容。自从我认识李以来，他一直失业，靠向一些朋友借钱生活。我不知道家里藏有共产主义文献。

pages.en:
Li Tsa Ming (李澤民) age 30.
Shantung. D.S. Sansom.
Hongkew Stn. 22/7/35. Clerk S. Y. Wong.

My name is Li Tsa Ming, age 30, native of Shantung, an unemployed school teacher, residing at No.79, Lane 426 North Kiangse Road.

I came to Shanghai from Chinen (濟南) Shantung on June 29, 1935 and went to reside at the aforementioned address. I came here on the advice of Wong Kwei Ming (王桂明) who promised me employment in a school.

I do not know where this friend resides; he met me on [illegible] a railway station on my arrival - I do not know which station or where it is located, and on the second occasion he visited me at my home. All the literature found at my residence was brought there by Wong Kwei Ming, native of Shantung, who instructed me to take care of it. All the furniture of the room also belongs to Wong. All the suit cases etc. belong to me. I brought to Shanghai $130.00 with me, which I had borrowed.

I graduated at the Ta Yoch Middle School (德育中学) in An Chow Hsien (安邱县) Shantung 9 years ago, then joined the army. On the downfall of Chang Tsung Chang (1927) I left the army and became a school teacher in the Wang Kuan Tun Primary School (王官屯小学) in Chi Hoen An Tseng (齊河晏城) Shantung, remaining there for about 8 years. Since then I have been unemployed and have lived on a bequest of $2,000.00 from my father. On coming to Shanghai I failed to obtain the employment promised me by Wong.

In March 1935, I began to cohabit with Ling Kwei Tsung (林桂貞) who to-day was arrested with me. Neither of us read any of the literature found at my home, but we knew that it was communistic in character.
pages.zh:
李泽民（Li Tsa Ming），30岁。
山东。D.S. Sansom。
虹口捕房 1935年7月22日。书记员 S. Y. Wong。

我叫李泽民，30岁，籍贯山东，是一名失业的教师，居住于北江西路426弄79号。

我于1935年6月29日从山东济南（Chinen）来到上海，并住进上述地址。我是听从王桂明（Wong Kwei Ming）的建议来这里的，他答应在学校给我安排工作。

我不知道这位朋友住在哪里；我到达时他在[原文不清]火车站接了我——我不知道是哪个车站，也不知道它位于何处，第二次是他到我家拜访我。在我住所发现的所有文献都是由山东人王桂明带去的，他指示我代为保管。房间里的所有家具也属于王。所有的手提箱等物品都属于我。我带到上海的130.00美元是我借来的。

9年前，我毕业于山东安丘县（An Chow Hsien）的德育中学（Ta Yoch Middle School），随后参军。在张宗昌（Chang Tsung Chang）垮台后（1927年），我离开了军队，成为山东齐河晏城（Chi Hoen An Tseng）（音译）王官屯小学（Wang Kuan Tun Primary School）的一名教师，在那里待了约8年。此后我一直失业，靠父亲遗留的2,000.00美元遗产生活。来到上海后，我未能获得王答应给我的工作。

1935年3月，我开始与林桂贞（Ling Kwei Tsung）同居，她今天与我一同被捕。我们没有阅读在我家发现的任何文献，但我们知道这些文献具有共产主义性质。

pages.en:
Li Tsa Ming (2).

We have no other friends in Shanghai.
Practically my time is spent at home.
pages.zh:
李泽民 (2)。

我们在上海没有其他朋友。
实际上我的时间都是在家里度过的。

Charge Application for writ of detention under Art. s 76 and 101 of C.C.P
Application is hereby made to the S.S.D. Court for the
detention for further enquiries of the above accused who
were arrested on 22/7/35 at Shanghai on suspicion of being concerned in communistic activities.

2nd Branch of Chinese High Court.
Mr. Lu appeared for the S.S.D.C.
PRO SECUTS. Mr. Liu applied for the detention of these accused
who were arrested at the request of Public Safety Bureau on search
warrant on suspicion of being concerned in communistic activities.
The 1st and 2nd accused are man and wife and they reside
at 5429 North Chungki Road. The 3rd accused is known as Lau Zih
as mentioned on the warrant. In the above mentioned house, one
room was found occupied by them and contained literature of communistic
nature. The 4th accused was arrested on Young Road, known as
Lau Jung. He stated that he is a stranger in Shanghai, but police
found his coat and tie by Shanghai tailor and he was also in possession
of communistic literature. The 4th & 5th accused were
arrested at 31 ... Road and a quantity of communistic literature
and cash money were seized in their house. I have here the statements
made by the accused produced.

1st accused:- I am not a member of communist. My friend
named Wong kept the literature in my home. I do not whereabouts of
him.

2nd accused:- I am not a communist. I married the 1st
accused in March last year.

3rd accused:- I just arrived at Shanghai yesterday to visit
my friend named Chiu in the Dah Woo Lodging House. I intent to go
back to Nanking last night.

4th accused:- I am not a communist. I know nothing about
the literature seized in my home.

指控 根据《刑事诉讼法》第76条和第101条申请拘留令
现向特区地方法院申请对上述被告进行拘留以作进一步调查，这些被告于1935年7月22日在上海因涉嫌参与共产主义活动而被捕。

江苏高等法院第二分院。
陆先生代表特区地方法院出庭。
公诉方。刘先生申请拘留这些被告，他们是应公安局的要求，凭搜查令因涉嫌参与共产主义活动而被捕的。
第一和第二被告是夫妻，他们居住在北中路5429号。第三被告如搜查令所述，又名刘子（Lau Zih）（音译）。在上述房屋中，发现有一个房间由他们占用，里面藏有共产主义性质的文献。第四被告在杨格路（Young Road）被捕，又名刘荣（Lau Jung）（音译）。他声称自己是上海的生客，但警察发现他的外套和领带是由上海裁缝制作的，而且他还持有共产主义文献。第四和第五被告在...路31号被捕，并在他们家中查获了大量共产主义文献和现金。我这里存有被告所作的供词。

第一被告：- 我不是共产党员。我的朋友王某将文献存放在我家中。我不知道他的下落。

第二被告：- 我不是共产党员。我于去年三月与第一被告结婚。

第三被告：- 我昨天刚到上海，去大吴旅馆（Dah Woo Lodging House）看望我的朋友邱某。我本打算昨晚回南京。

第四被告：- 我不是共产党员。我对在我家查获的文献一无所知。

2nd Branch of Shanghai High Court
Mr. Pu appeared for the Shanghai Municipal Council.

PROCEEDINGS.
Mr. Wu:- The 1st and 3rd accused were arrested at house
No. 9 Lane 432 North Kiangsi Road and pro-communist literatures were
also seized in their house. When the 3rd accused was arrested,
nothing was found in his possession. At the Police Station he tried
to destroy the evidence by eating it. The 2nd and 4th accused were arrested at the corner of Nanking Road and where in a
house known as the residence of one of the leaders of the Communist Party of China.
It is alleged that they are members of the Communist Party and that they were arrested by the 2nd
Branch in connection with this case. It is further alleged that the
evidence against them is sufficient to justify their detention.

I ask the Court to give an order for the disposal of
the properties now confiscated, including those at No. 9 Lane 432
North Kiangsi Road and those at the other place.

Witness, Tsang Yih stated: I identify the 3rd accused being
a member of communist and his real name is called Yih. I do not
know what was his position in the communist party.

3rd accused:- I am not a member of communist. I don't
know the man who is called Yih.

1st accused:- Our properties to be kept by the chief tenant
for safe custody.

4th accused:- My wife, the 5th accused is not a communist.
I ask the Court to release her and she will disposed of the property.

Summing up:-

DECISION.
2nd & 4th accused to be released immediately as they are
not to be handed over.
1st, 3rd & 5th accused to be handed over to the Shanghai
Public Safety Bureau together with the exhibits.

Tang.

页码 4
上海高等法院第二分院
浦先生代表上海公共租界工部局出庭。

诉讼程序。
吴先生：- 第一和第三被告在北江西路432弄9号的房屋内被捕，并在他们家中查获了亲共文献。第三被告被捕时，身上未搜出任何物品。在捕房里，他试图通过吞食证据来销毁证据。第二和第四被告在南京路拐角处的一栋房屋内被捕，该房屋据称是中国共产党某位领导人的住所。
据称他们是共产党员，并且第二分院因本案将他们逮捕。还据称针对他们的证据足以证明拘留他们的合理性。

我请求法院下令处置目前没收的财产，包括北江西路432弄9号的财产以及其他地方的财产。

证人张义（Tsang Yih）陈述：我指认第三被告是共产党员，他的真名叫义（Yih）。我不知道他在共产党内的职位是什么。

第三被告：- 我不是共产党员。我不认识那个叫义的人。

第一被告：- 我们的财产由二房东保管以确保安全。

第四被告：- 我的妻子，即第五被告，不是共产党员。我请求法院释放她，她将处理这些财产。

总结：-

决定。
第二和第四被告立即释放，因为他们不予移交。
第一、第三和第五被告连同证物一并移交给上海公安局。

唐。

He also stated that the 1st accused, and 2nd accused had requested to him that the household furniture of their houses be handed over to the Public Safety Bureau.

D.S.I. Chu Meng Wei accompanied this detective to Nantao and there received confirmation of this request.

At 3p.m. 1/8/35 the above Public Safety Bureau detective together with the undersigned and D.S.I. Chu Meng Wei visited 29/648 Ferry Road, the home of the 1st accused and 85/1000 Gordon Road, the home of the 2nd and 3rd accused, and there made a check of all property therein. (Copy attached).

In the home of the 2nd and 3rd accused was a Siamese Amah and through the medium of an interpreter named, "Ting Mah Tseng" (丁克昌 ) residing in a pawnshop off Connaught Road, it was learned that she was one named, "Lieu Eung Sa" (刘陳氏 ) aged 58, and had with her, her two sons, Lieu Ching Tsung (刘锦章 ) aged 11, and Lieu Sen Ying (刘素英 ) aged 8 years, this woman it was learned was the mother of the 3rd accused, having been in Shanghai only a very short time.

1935年7月31日下午2时，隶属于南市公安局总部的梅子章（Mei Tse Zang）督察来到警局，被移交的被告的证物和个人财产交由其保管，并在扣押登记簿上签收。

他还表示，第1被告和第2被告曾请求他将他们家中的家具移交给公安局。

副督察朱孟伟（Chu Meng Wei）陪同这名警探前往南市，并在那里确认了这一请求。

1935年8月1日下午3时，上述公安局警探会同签署人及副督察朱孟伟访问了第1被告的住所斐伦路648弄29号，以及第2和第3被告的住所戈登路1000弄85号，并在那里清点了所有财产。（附副本）。

在第2和第3被告的家中有一名暹罗籍女佣，通过居住在康纳脱路（Connaught Road）外一家当铺的一名名叫“丁克昌”的翻译得知，她名叫“刘陳氏”，58岁，身边带着两个儿子，刘锦章（11岁）和刘素英（8岁），据悉这名妇女是第3被告的母亲，来上海时间很短。
